Inanda Land Grab

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Small scale farmers in Inanda KZN have been affected by land invasion.

Unique Selling Point:
50 Small scale farmers in Tea Estate in the Inanda area, woke up one morning to find their farms invaded and people marking plots to start construction of informal dwellings. According to the invaders the local chief of the Qadi tribe,Induna MB Ngcobo, sold the land to invaders for R30 000 to R40 000 per plot. The farmers have title deeds to the 10 hectares of land that they own individually. According to the chief, title deeds do not authorize their ownership and that the land all the way to Umhlanga belongs to him and the tribe.

Summary:
In latest developments land invaders have now occupied homes on two farms.
The Umhlodi Farmers Association has taken the matter to the High Court. The case has been postponed till the 23rd of March.
Last week in his address to traditional leaders, President Ramaphosa said that they played a crucial role in land reform. The question is if traditional leaders have the right to sell land owned by farmers for personal gain? Chief Ngcobo seems to think that he has jurisdiction over the land . Rumour has it that he has a gambling problem and is funding it through the sale of the land. Farmers have complained that he has tremendous influence in the area and even the SAPS Land Invasion Unit not been able to stop the land grab.

Press Release:


Inanda Land Feuds
A major standoff has been brewing between small-scale farmers in the Inanda area of KwaZulu-Natal and the local chief. The chief insists the land the farms are on, as well as all surrounding land, belongs to him, which gives him the right to sell off portions as he pleases. Title deeds, the chief insists, do not necessarily denote ownership. For the past two years about 50 farms have been invaded by people who were starting to construct dwellings on their farms, claiming they’d paid up to R40 000 for their plots. The Umdloti Farmers Association has meanwhile taken the matter to the High Court. What’s really behind land invasions in Inanda?


Script:


Inanda Land Grab

Drone Shot

Macfarlane Link Land reform and the distribution of land is a highly emotional and contentious issue… But nowhere is it more contentious and volatile than here in KZN, Inanda

V/O For the past two years, a group of small-scale sugarcane and vegetable farmers in Tea Estate Inanda near Durban, have had their land invaded, their workers intimidated and crops destroyed by people who claim to have bought plots of land from the Qadi chief in the area..

Willie Naicker:

Chairperson: Umdloti Farmers

Association Late 2015 we had a protest march in our area, in Tea Estate Inanda area, where the chief claims that it's his land and … and stopped the farmers from entering the farms. Ever since then there was continuous land invasion in our area.

V/O Chairperson of the Umdloti Farmers Association, Willie Naicker, has been acting as spokesperson for the affected farmers in the area.

Willie Naicker They come, the Indunas come with vehicles, 3, 4 vehicles. They start pegging the land and marking sites for people. On a Friday, Saturday, Sunday it's like Wakefields in our property where they getting people coming and buying land.

V/O

Freddy Govender is a third generation Tea Estate farmer. His grandfather bought the farm in 1933 and for 85 years the Govenders’ have been cultivating the land.

Freddy Govender:

Farmer This for me started in 2017 when the locals came on board with the Indunas to say this is their land. They have been directed here by the chief and sights have been cut and demarcated and lots of damage done to my fields, the very crop has been removed by the roots. To fix this... ag I've lost my plot I don't want agriculture. I have lived a happy life here until this has happened.

V/O Having lived amicably with the local community for many years, the invasion of their land came as a shock to these small scale farmers.

Harry Moodley:

Farmer From October last year we found that the sugar cane was cut, poles were erected and plots were demarcated. And within a few weeks we found that foundations were dug and then the dwellings were coming up.

Bob Govender

Farmer Last week Wednesday, about midday, about 10 o'clock, I seen a yellow tractor. What was the yellow tractor doing? Grading the soil. What was here before? Marigolds.Full marigolds are here.

V/O The Govenders are fearful and concerned about their future.

Bob Govender They are worried, every day they phone us. Especially my daughter works in a bank. Keep phoning, phoning and asking how we are. I am sorry I really hope that you can get help. Thank you so much. I really hope your family will be okay.

V/O

Driving along Harry Moodley’s farm we came across an elderly man clearing sugarcane.

Land invader 00004610 So you also bought a place? Yes I did. I bought it at emaQadini at the Chief's place 00013014 So how much did you pay? R25,000. As you can see from there to there the one I have already cut. 00014418 So who did you give the money to?

It’s the headman who came and showed me the place. 00024503 So for R25000 how much hectares you get. From there to there. Who measured it for you? The Induna, headman.

Harry Moodley We've been to the police. They were not prepared to take a statement from us. All they told us was that the land is in dispute and we just had to leave. We went on several occasions to the police station. Right now the income is zero from this farm simply because the workers that were on this farm were intimidated, they were actually threatened. They had to leave.

V/O Over 800 farmworkers have been affected by the land invasions. Libalele Gwazi, has worked on one of these farms for more than 20 years.

Libalele Gwazi:

Farmworker 02583109 Yes It was fine when I started working here. Things started changing last year when we started being abused and told we must leave our jobs. 02583815 Who is abusing you? People from the community. The headman. Why are they saying you should go? You must go back to the Eastern Cape because this is their land. 03021214 The Induna came and chased us away from the field. And said this place that we're in is theirs. 03021802 We said we're not going to go because we're here to work for our children. 03022422 And he said he's going to shoot one Pondo.

V/O While interviewing Mr Moodley on his farm we were suddenly ambushed by Induna , forced into our cars and driven to what turned out to be the tribal court of Qadi Chief

Ngcobo. There were interrogated by the Chief and his Induna on why we were trespassing on his land. We were told that a vast area of land, stretching from Inanda to Durban is Qadi tribal land, all belonging to Chief Ngcobo and the Qadi people. More than an hour later we told to leave and that we could return at a later date for an on-camera interview.

V/O After hours of intense negotiation with the Inkosi and his Induna, Carte Blanche was eventually granted and interview ..

MB Ngcobo

Qadi Chief 07595818 This land is the land of emaQadini and was given by Ingonyama Trust.

V/O The chief then continued to say that ownership of land is not determined by title deeds.

MB Ngcobo

08061103; We don’t know what this animal is,(Title deeds) even our grandfathers have never seen it.

Freddy Govender He says that we are only farmers, we are not land owners. And our parents were here farming the land. But his ancestors owned the land. Where were they when we came aboard? The idea of title deeds doesn't stand, doesn't stand at all with him. He doesn't want to hear of a title deed.

Freddy Govender The Nkosi has said he'll demarcate a site for me on my own farm and it will be a residential site. It will not be the hectares I have farmed. And I cannot lay claim to this land, it is his land.

Chief Ngcobo 08043316 But I want those farmers to lead the same lives under my chieftaincy on my land. 08044417 So a person must own 50m2 08045320 Just like any other person, even the Indian should have 50m2. The Indian shouldn't have a place from here to Inanda. 08050110 It shouldn’t' be a place from here to Inanda and Kwamashu, why is that? 08050802 Which human rights are given to the Indian? 08051509 What kind of South Africa that has to have people who are better than others? 08052701 I want the people of emaQadi to enjoy the fruits of their land.

V/O After the Land Act was promulgated in 1913 and during the apartheid years many traditional leaders were not recognised and were called landless chiefs. And thus it is crucial for these tribal leaders like Chief Ncgobo, to establish a land base in order to assert their authority.

Aninka Claasens

Director:Land and

Accountability Research

Center UCT In terms of customary law traditional leaders do not just allocate land willy nilly its allocated though a process of local consultation and consent but what we are seeing here is a traditional leader allocating it willy nilly and allocating land that actually belongs to other people. As I understand the people who’s land is being sold are Indian farmers and the tragedy is that often when it happens it is Coloured or Indian land owners who are targeted. And there are other instances where there had been a complete failure of the state to protect their land rights.

V/O

Dr Aninka Claasens is the Director of the Land and Accountability Research Centre at the University of Cape Town and has been engaged in land issues for 25 years.

Dr Aninka Claasens:

This is not to say that this land has not been historically land owned by the Qadi community but what we need are processes of proper restitution and redistribution for change to take place in an orderly way and we have seen an enormous failure by government to bring about effective land reform. Which then creates this context in which this kind of people take power into their own hand and you have a complete breakdown of the rule of law.

V/O

KZN MEC for Agriculture and Rural Development, Themba Mthembu says a breakdown in the rule of law will not be allowed.

Themba Mthembu:

KZN MEC for Agriculture &

Rural Development Obviously we cannot sit aside and idle when such unfortunate incidents happen. As the Department, we have already sent a team there of officials, we'll be looking at the report and we will be approaching first the Nkosi involved, which is Nkosi XX. And we'll also be speaking to the police. And we have also to speak to the owners of that land.

It's only that it’s happening silently. Also that's

why we need to praise investigative journalists also for bringing these things up because some of them will happen under our nose and we don't realise them. So definitely we need to sit down and speak with those farmers and see that they do get protection from the government.

V/O But according to Yaga Govender, President of the Natal Cane Growers Association , no government structure has come forward and given any of these farmers a reprieve or assistance.

Yaga Govender:

President : Natal Cane

Growers Association. Mr Mtembu has assured us that the matter will be resolved via his head of department and his HOD made a few phone calls to us saying that he would like to meet us. Subsequently after calling him so many times a meeting has never materialised.

The way forward is now that we have taken the matter to court and the last thread that we have to hang onto is the constitutional law of this country.

V/O While Tea Estate farmers are waiting for intervention by either government or the High Court, they are left feeling helpless and afraid of what the future will bring.

Freddy Govender I cannot see this thing being resolved easily in the sense that the kind of damage we have incurred – Currently with things like this happening it leaves a sad thought, a bitter taste, it leaves you that you need to walk away. It's come to that time now. This has wrecked our lands, taking our livelihood away. There is no tomorrow for me and my staff and my family on this specific land.

Promo 15” Since early 2015 farms in Kzn have been invaded by people claiming to have bought the land from the local chief. Crops have been destroyed and farmworkers intimidated. Up sound

Promo 15’’ With their land invaded , crops destroyed and

workers intimidated, farmers in Inanda Kwazulu Natal face a bleak future.

Promo 10’’ For the past two years, small scale sugarcane and vegetable farmers in Inanda KZN have been in a major stand-of with the local chief.
